anchors.description: Vertical distance through the glazed double entrance door from the inner lower edge of the head frame to the door threshold at the same image column (x=800).
anchors.visible_evidence: Bright door head frame inner edge at y=303.5 and the leaf bottom rail / threshold line at y=600 in the same column; the two leaves and frame lie in the facade glazing plane, camera horizon is well below the head.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Exact door model unknown; European commercial entrance doors have clear passage heights of about 2.0-2.3 m. This working length is also the scale assumption behind the planar-facade calibration, so absolute scale is uncertain at the 5-8 percent level.

anchors.description: Horizontal distance at mid-door height between the centreline of the hinge-side outer stile and the centreline of the right end stile of the double-leaf entrance door.
anchors.visible_evidence: Two bright vertical stiles bound the leaf pair; subpixel centres x=648 and x=856.5 at y=520; the measured leaf modules are 0.82 and 0.85 m, matching the standard 860 mm leaf module of double-leaf doors (two modules give about 1.72 m overall).
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Leaf module not verified as DIN 18101; the measured 0.81-0.85 m per leaf suggests 860 mm nominal, but 735 mm or 985 mm variants would give 1.47 m or 1.97 m overall, so roughly 5-8 percent spread around the claimed span.

anchors.description: Vertical diameter of the round prohibition sign (red ring, blue disc, red diagonal) mounted on the concrete pier left of the entrance.
anchors.visible_evidence: Subpixel top and bottom edges of the disc at y=395.1 and y=429.9 on column x=509.6 (34.8 px tall, 26.4 px wide, consistent with a circular disc seen obliquely); mounted on the pier face which stands slightly in front of the glazing plane.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Sign class is a German-style Haltverbot/no-stopping disc; road-sign sizes are 420 or 600 mm, but the calibrated facade scale (door height) implies a small private-property variant near 300 mm. Pier standoff of roughly 0.2-0.5 m adds about 5 percent size uncertainty.
